documents.subject: Price adjustment from 01 January 2027
documents.author: Platinenwerk Lausitz GmbH
documents.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,
we have supplied Hollerau Pumpenwerke reliably for many years. Owing to the strong rise in copper and electronic component prices, we are forced to adjust our prices for Control board HB smart pump (PCBA) (part:350030) by **8.0 %** with effect from **01 January 2027**: from EUR 34.35 to EUR 37.10 per  pc.
We regret this step and ask for your understanding.
Yours faithfully,
Platinenwerk Lausitz GmbH

documents.subject: Annual review
documents.author: Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing
documents.text: Annual review with Platinenwerk Lausitz GmbH. Their key account manager explained that price changes above 2 % need the approval of their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.

persona.summary: Platinenwerk Lausitz GmbH, privately owned PCBA maker (320 staff); we are 0.72 % of its turnover; it is our sole source for the smart-pump control board. It asks +8.0 % (34.35 to 37.10), citing copper and electronics; notice was on time. It has sold below full cost for four years to keep the volume (should-cost 37.24). Concede part of the increase, but use its poor quality and our volume.
persona.notes: Needs volume; it fears losing the part. Quality is weak: 21 complaints in three years, ppm up to 701, two open 8D, OTD 84-92 %. We pay late (40.6 % of invoices over 5 days), though it has not complained yet. Squeezing below its cost is risky with no second source.

avoid: copper or electronics index arguments (they rose)
threatening a second source we do not have
claiming a notice breach (letter on time)
tactics: Open moderately, at or just above 34.35; it is below cost and we have no second source.
Lead with the quality record: open 8D reports, rising ppm and 21 complaints.
Offer a binding annual volume; it has always traded price to keep the volume.
Aim to settle below its 2 % committee threshold (about 35.0).
playbook.expected_concession: No arena data; history shows it settles well below its ask (last year asked 2.1 %, settled 0.4 %), so expect it to give up most of the 8 %.
